title: Property Developer Salary: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert a property developer salary from hourly to annual using a 38-hour week, plus tax and super estimates based on Fair Work and ATO data.
salarySummary: For a property developer earning an hourly rate under the Real Estate Industry Award, the annual salary is the hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the typical hourly rate for a property developer?
faqs.a: Property developer salaries vary widely by role and experience. Under the Real Estate Industry Award, a Level 3 (Supervisory Level) employee earns $1,231.00 per week, which is about $32.39 per hour for a 38-hour week. However, many property developers are award-free or covered by enterprise agreements, so market rates may be higher. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 (May 2026), which equates to roughly $54.83 per hour.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to a property developer salary?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the Real Estate Industry Award receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For example, a Level 2 casual employee earning the minimum $29.45 per hour would get $36.73 per hour. When using the timesheet tool, you can check the 'casual loading box to add this loading on top of the base rate. The loading is paid for all purposes and replaces entitlements like annual leave and sick leave.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual gross pay from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a full-time employee on 38 hours, it's hourly × 38 × 52. For a fortnight, multiply the weekly amount by 2. Superannuation is paid on top at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Tax is deducted using the 2026–27 resident rates: nil up to $18,200, then 15%, 30%, 37%, and 45% for higher brackets, plus a 2% Medicare levy.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting a Property Developer Salary from Hourly to Annual

If you work in property development and are paid by the hour, or you're considering a salary offer, understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential. This guide explains the conversion using a standard 38-hour week, the 52-week year, and includes estimates for tax and superannuation based on figures from the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Australian Bureau of Statistics, and the Australian Taxation Office.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a full-time employee working 38 ordinary hours each week, that's:

**Annual = hourly × 38 × 52**

For example, if your hourly rate is $40.00:
- Weekly: $40 × 38 = $1,520.00
- Fortnightly: $1,520 × 2 = $3,040.00
- Annual: $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040.00

This formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It's a starting point for comparing offers.

### Property Developer Salary Under Awards and Market Rates

Property developers may be covered by the Real Estate Industry Award 2020 [MA000106] if they perform real estate work such as selling, leasing, or managing property. The award sets minimum weekly rates for different classification levels. For instance, a Real Estate Employee Level 3 (Supervisory Level) earns $1,231.00 per week as of 1 July 2026, which is about $32.39 per hour (). However, many property developers are not covered by this award; they may be award-free or covered by an enterprise agreement. In those cases, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week) applies as a floor ().

For a more market-based view, the Australian Bureau of Statistics' Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 shows full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, or roughly $54.83 per hour. That figure includes all industries and occupations, so a property developer's actual rate could be higher or lower depending on experience and location.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you work as a casual property developer, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. Under the Real Estate Industry Award, the casual loading is included in the all-purpose rate (). When using the timesheet tool, you can check the 'casual loading' box to add this 25% on top of the base hourly rate you enter. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on an annual salary of $79,040, the super contribution would be $9,484.80 (12% of $79,040). This is not deducted from your pay; it's paid separately by your employer.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). The total tax and Medicare are deducted from your gross pay to give an estimate of take-home pay. Remember, this estimate does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Using the Timesheet and Other Tools

To quickly convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, or weekly figures, use [the timesheet](/) on this site. You can also explore [pay guides](/blog) for award-specific rates, or check [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) for more examples. For a property developer salary, always confirm your classification and any applicable award or agreement with your employer or the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Summary

Converting a property developer salary from hourly to annual is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by 38 (hours per week) and then by 52 (weeks per year). Add casual loading if applicable, and remember that super is paid on top. Tax and Medicare reduce your take-home pay. Use the tools on this site to get a quick estimate, but for precise figures, consult a tax professional or the Fair Work Ombudsman.
